summary: Completed testing of template editing features, Apply to Devices functionality, dashboard stats, device filtering, and alert notification tracking. All 7 features tested are working correctly.
passed_tests: 1. Template Editing: Edit dialog opens with inline OID editing (Name, OID, Type, Unit, Operator, Warning/Critical thresholds)
2. Template Save: Modified threshold value from 70 to 75 and back - changes persisted correctly
3. Apply to Devices: Button works, shows success toast 'Template applied to X devices'
4. Alert Notifications: Code review confirms tracking of shown alert IDs (shownAlertIds ref) to prevent duplicate toasts
5. Dashboard: Loads with stats cards (Total Devices, Online, Offline, Active Alerts), Device Status list, Active Alerts panel, Pinned Graphs, Devices by Category
6. Device Filtering: Clicking 'Offline' card navigates to /devices?status=offline with filter indicator
7. Templates Page: Shows templates grouped by brand (Cisco, Ubiquiti, Mikrotik, Generic) with Edit/Delete/Apply buttons
backend_tests_passed: PUT /api/templates/{id} - Update template with OID threshold changes
POST /api/templates/{id}/apply-to-devices - Apply template to linked devices
critical_code_review_comments: Alert notification tracking implemented correctly using shownAlertIds ref to prevent duplicate toasts
Device status change tracking uses previousDeviceStatuses ref to show online/offline transitions only once
Template OID updates propagate correctly to devices via apply-to-devices endpoint
seed_data_creation: None - used existing seed data from previous iteration
context_for_next_testing_agent: Template editing with inline OID modification fully functional. Apply to Devices propagates template changes to linked devices. Alert notification deduplication working via shownAlertIds tracking. Dashboard clickable filters navigate to filtered device views. All SNMP polling is REAL (not mocked) using pysnmp library - devices show OFFLINE because IPs are simulated (192.168.x.x, 10.0.0.x, 172.16.x.x).

mocked_api.note: SNMP and Ping polling is REAL using pysnmp and subprocess ping - devices appear OFFLINE because seed data uses non-existent IPs
